+    ImageMagick chooses a coder from the content of the file it is given, and
+    some coders act on files named inside the image rather than on the image
+    itself. Active Storage constrained none of them, so an uploaded file could
+    reach any coder the host's policy allowed, through the ImageMagick analyzer
+    at attach time, with no variant or `analyze` call in the application.
+    Active Storage now ships a `policy.xml` in
+    every policy file on its search path, so the shipped policy adds to the
+    host's policy rather than replacing it. A `MAGICK_CONFIGURE_PATH` set in the
+    environment or in `MiniMagick.cli_env`, including by an initializer or
+    dotenv, is kept after the shipped directory.
+    The shipped policy denies the coders that script ImageMagick (`MSL`), read
+    or delete files other than the image (`TEXT`, `EPHEMERAL`), fetch remote
+    `WIN`, `PLT`), or hand the file to Ghostscript (the `PS`, `EPS`, `EPT` and
+    `PDF` coders, every alias of them, and the `gs` delegate), or reach a file
+    indirection. The policy applies to every ImageMagick command MiniMagick
+    *   One whose variant processor is `:mini_magick` has to use mini_magick 5.1
+        or later, which applying the policy requires. With an older mini_magick,
+    *   One that renders PostScript or PDF through ImageMagick has to re-allow
+        the `gs` delegate and the coders it uses in the host's `policy.xml`. A
+        host policy that allows a coder overrides the shipped deny.
+    *   One that replaces `MiniMagick.cli_env` after it boots, clears the
+        environment with `MiniMagick.cli_prefix`, or installs its own
+        `MiniMagick::Shell` never receives the shipped policy and has to carry
+        its rules in ImageMagick's system policy. So does one that uses
+        GraphicsMagick, which does not read ImageMagick policies.
+    Every other application needs no change. See "ImageMagick Security Policy"

+  Active Storage's ImageMagick security policy. Applied in addition to the host's policy.xml,
+  through MAGICK_CONFIGURE_PATH, to every ImageMagick process MiniMagick spawns.
+  This file must work under both ImageMagick 6 and ImageMagick 7. Use the "coder", "delegate"
+  and "path" domains, which every release of both honors. A domain one release does not know,
+  such as "module" on older ImageMagick 6 releases, is ignored rather than rejected.
+  ImageMagick picks a coder from the file's content, and several coders name the same underlying
+  reader through different tokens (PS, EPS, EPI, EPSF, EPSI, EPT; PDF, AI, EPDF, PDFA, POCKETMOD). A
+  coder rule matches one token, so every token is denied by coder.
+  Do not put a backtick anywhere in this file. ImageMagick's tokenizer treats a backtick as an
+  opening quote and silently drops every rule up to the next apostrophe.
+  <!-- Scripting coder that reads and writes files named inside the image. -->

+  <!-- Coder that reads back a pixel cache from a file the image header names. -->
+  <!-- Coders that display to a screen. -->
+  <!-- Coders that read a reference from outside the image, remote or local. FILE reads file://. -->
+  <!-- Interpreters that read and write files of their own. Ghostscript backs the PS and PDF
+       coders and their token aliases; GhostXPS and GhostPCL back XPS and PCL. The "gs" delegate
+       covers ImageMagick builds that run Ghostscript as an external command, and the coder rules
+       cover builds that link it in-process, where the delegate rule never applies. An
+       application that transforms PostScript or PDF through ImageMagick must allow the "gs"

+  <!-- Indirect reads such as text:@/etc/passwd, which substitute a file for an argument. -->
+  test "analyzing raises when mini_magick cannot apply the security policy" do

+  test "every Ghostscript-backed coder is denied by coder" do

+Active Storage ships an ImageMagick security policy, in
+`ActiveStorage::ImageMagick::POLICY_DIRECTORY`, that denies coders untrusted uploads must not reach.
+It prepends that directory to `MAGICK_CONFIGURE_PATH` through `MiniMagick.cli_env`, so every
+ImageMagick process MiniMagick spawns applies it. ImageMagick applies every `policy.xml` on its
+search path, so the shipped policy adds to your system policy rather than replacing it, and a
+`MAGICK_CONFIGURE_PATH` you set, in the environment or in `MiniMagick.cli_env`, stays on the
+search path after it. Active Storage applies the policy again after your application initializes,
+so a value an initializer or dotenv sets is kept too. ImageMagick policies are
+blocklists, so expect Active Storage to maintain and expand the shipped file over time.
+Because `MAGICK_CONFIGURE_PATH` is set in `MiniMagick.cli_env` rather than the shell, list the
+policy through MiniMagick to see what your application actually loads:
+Applying the policy requires mini_magick 5.1 or later. With an older mini_magick, an application
+whose variant processor is `:mini_magick` raises at boot.
+The shipped policy reaches only ImageMagick processes started through MiniMagick with its default
+shell. If your application replaces `MiniMagick.cli_env` after it boots, clears the environment with
+`MiniMagick.cli_prefix`, or installs its own `MiniMagick::Shell`, it does not receive the shipped
+policy: copy its rules into a policy in ImageMagick's system location, such as
+`/etc/ImageMagick-7/policy.xml`. That is also where any stricter rules of your own belong.

+The shipped policy sets no resource limits. ImageMagick takes each limit from the first policy on
